title: Research Licensing Requirements
description: Understand the specific licensing requirements for your childcare center type in Michigan
why: Each type of childcare facility has different requirements. Understanding these upfront helps you plan and budget effectively.
how: Visit the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA) website, review the Child Care Licensing Rules, and consult with local licensing consultants if needed.

title: Develop Business Plan
description: Create a comprehensive business plan including financial projections and operational procedures
why: A solid business plan is essential for securing funding and demonstrates your preparedness to licensing authorities.
how: Include market analysis, financial projections, staffing plans, curriculum development, and emergency procedures.

title: Secure and Prepare Facility
description: Find and prepare a suitable location that meets all licensing requirements
why: The facility must meet specific safety, space, and accessibility requirements before you can apply for a license.
how: Find a location, ensure it meets space requirements (35 sq ft per child indoors, 75 sq ft outdoors), check zoning compliance, and plan necessary renovations.

title: Fire Safety Inspection
description: Schedule and pass a fire safety inspection with your local fire department
why: Fire safety compliance is mandatory for all childcare facilities and must be completed before licensing.
how: Contact your local fire department to schedule an inspection. Ensure all fire safety equipment is installed and functioning properly.

title: Health Department Inspection
description: Schedule and pass a health department inspection
why: Health and sanitation standards must be met to ensure the safety of children in your care.
how: Contact your local health department to schedule an inspection. Ensure proper sanitation, food handling, and health safety measures are in place.

title: Complete Background Checks
description: Complete criminal background checks for all staff and household members
why: All individuals who will have contact with children must pass comprehensive background checks.
how: Submit fingerprint cards and background check forms for all staff members and household members over 18.

title: Complete Required Staff Training
description: Ensure all staff complete required training including CPR, First Aid, and child development
why: Staff must be properly trained to ensure the safety and development of children in your care.
how: Schedule and complete CPR/First Aid certification, child development training, and any other required training programs.

title: Develop Educational Curriculum
description: Create age-appropriate educational curriculum and daily schedules
why: A structured curriculum demonstrates your commitment to child development and is required for licensing.
how: Develop age-appropriate activities, learning objectives, and daily schedules that promote child development.

title: Submit Licensing Application
description: Complete and submit your official licensing application to LARA
why: This is the formal application that starts the official licensing process.
how: Complete all required forms, gather supporting documentation, and submit to LARA with appropriate fees.

title: Licensing Inspection
description: Pass the final licensing inspection conducted by LARA
why: This is the final step before receiving your license to operate.
how: Prepare your facility for inspection, ensure all requirements are met, and work with the licensing specialist to address any issues.

title: Enroll in Great Start to Quality
description: Enroll your program in Michigan's Great Start to Quality rating system
why: Great Start to Quality provides quality improvement support and can increase your program's visibility to families.
how: Complete the Great Start to Quality enrollment process, which includes a self-assessment and quality improvement planning.

title: Apply for Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
description: Apply for CACFP if you plan to serve meals to children
why: CACFP provides reimbursement for nutritious meals and snacks, helping to offset food costs.
how: Complete the CACFP application process, which includes menu planning and nutrition education requirements.
